title: Load a flask onto a rotary evaporator: seat its socket on the tilted cone, clamp it, lower it into the bath
instruction: Put the flask of extract on the rotary evaporator, clamped, and lower it into the water bath, ready to run; then return both arms to where they started.
context: Rotary evaporation is how synthetic chemistry and analytical labs strip solvent from a solution, many times a day, and the flask is loaded by hand every time. The maker's procedure (Heidolph Hei-VAP operating instructions): with the lift at its upper end, place the flask so that the ground joints of the flask and the vapor tube are fully aligned in a straight line, press the EASY CLIP's clamping lever over the flask collar until it audibly clicks into place, then move the lift down; mishandled, the evaporation flask can fall. The skill is physical: the flask's socket has to go onto a ground cone that points down at 30 degrees, moved straight along that axis, and be held home there by one hand while the other shuts the clamp, because a dry ground joint does not carry the flask on that slope.
setup: A table (the arms' deck) in front of two arms (bases 61 cm apart), seen by one overhead camera and a camera on each wrist. Distances are measured forward from the line between the arm bases and sideways from the midpoint between them; heights from the deck. (1) The lab bench: a black epoxy bench top 60 mm below the deck, filling a cut-out in it from 9 to 80 cm forward and from 22 cm right to 16 cm left (the arms stand on a 60 mm plinth at the bench). (2) On it, a benchtop rotary evaporator, Heidolph Hei-VAP Core type with motor lift and vertical G3 glassware, facing the arms: the white base unit at the back (47 to 70 cm forward, 26 cm wide), its lift column at 60 to 69 cm, and the rotary head on the lift carrying the drive housing, the vertical glass condenser (40 cm tall, 9 cm across) with its receiving flask, and the glass vapour tube. The tube's axis points toward the arms and down, 30 degrees below horizontal; it ends in an NS 24/40 ground cone (frosted glass, 40 mm long, 24 to 20 mm across) whose base is 36.3 cm forward on the centre line, 149 mm above the deck, with the lift at its upper end. On the tube just behind the cone sits the EASY CLIP flask clamp (blue plastic): a ring with a 36 mm clamping lever hinged on its top and a hook at the lever's tip; the lever is open, raised 35 degrees. The lift has 95 mm of travel down to its immersion stop and moves at 25 mm/s while a lift key is held. (3) The heating bath on the base unit's plate, centred 29.2 cm forward on the centre line: a stainless steel pot 253 mm across inside and 291 mm outside, its rim 60 mm above the deck, holding 3.0 L of water whose surface is 25 mm above the deck. (4) The evaporator's control panel on the deck: a dark grey console 14 x 12 x 4.5 cm centred 17.5 cm forward and 23.5 cm left, with a display and the lift's two keys (16 mm white caps standing 12 mm proud): DOWN at 14.5 cm forward and 25.7 cm left, UP at 14.5 cm forward and 21.3 cm left. (5) The flask: a 100 mL round-bottom borosilicate glass flask with an NS 24/40 socket: a 64 mm bulb, a neck 30 mm across and 52 mm long, a 34 mm bead round its mouth, 114 mm tall; with its 40 mL of amber extract it weighs 0.10 kg. It stands upright in a cork ring (90 mm outside, 50 mm inside, 25 mm tall) on the deck, centred 32 cm forward and 22 cm left. Fixed: everything but the flask, the rotary head (on the lift), the clamp's lever (on its hinge) and the two keys. The layout is the same in every trial, as in the screenshot. Real trial: a working lab's rotary evaporator (a Hei-VAP Core with motor lift, or any model whose flask clamp clicks over the flask's collar and whose lift runs on keys) with vacuum, rotation and bath heating off, tilt 30 degrees, immersion stop 95 mm below the top, the bath left dry; a plastic-coated 100 mL NS 24/40 round-bottom safety flask (a dropped one does not break) holding 40 mL of water tinted with food colouring, which stays in the bulb; the grippers touch only the flask's dry outside; a cork ring.
scoring: Latched for the rest of the trial: 0.0 once the flask has been dropped: off the cone and fallen below 35 mm above the deck outside its cork ring (into the bath, onto the bench or the deck). Otherwise judged at the end of the trial, on live states: 1.0: the flask home on the vapour tube's cone (its mouth within 4 mm of the cone's base), the EASY CLIP clicked shut over its collar, the lift down at its immersion stop (within 4 mm), so the bulb sits in the bath's water, and both arms back where they started (each gripper's fingertip centre within 5 cm of its start); 0.75: the same with an arm not back; 0.5: the flask home and clamped, the lift not down; 0.25: the flask on the cone (its socket onto it), not clamped; else 0.0. The clamp clicks shut only when its lever is pressed to within 3 degrees of shut with the socket home; pressed earlier, its hook lands on the collar or it springs back open. The trial ends at the run limit, or once the full score has held for 1 s with the flask, the head and the lever still. In a real trial: home: no frosted cone shows between the flask's collar and the clamp ring (a close photo with a ruler: gap within 4 mm); clamped: the lever lies flat on the joint with its hook behind the collar and stays shut when let go (photo; the click is heard); lift down: the lift's carriage against its immersion stop and the bulb inside the bath below its rim (photo); on the cone: the socket over the cone (photo); dropped: the trial video shows the flask off the cone, falling. The arms are checked against marks at their start.
reset_notes: Lift up (UP key held), open the EASY CLIP's lever, hold the flask, ease it off the cone along the axis and stand it back in its cork ring.
fidelity: Rigid-body simulation (Isaac Sim, PhysX, 20 Hz), real sizes. The ground joint is a catch: within 5.5 mm and 10 degrees of the cone's axis a joint lets the socket only slide along and turn about it; unclamped, gravity and 3 N s/m of joint friction act, so a flask let go slides off. The clamp's click is a rule: its lever latches within 3 degrees of shut with the socket home. The lift is a slide driven at 25 mm/s while a key is held. The water is drawn only. Cameras 1280x704 (Dream-1: 320x176).
